svg.text: VLA v583 — one clock tick (40 ms): a ConvDelta language model, 7 blocks of per-tick convs, each followed by a gated delta-rule memory per grid position

A · the whole model. --lm: text only · C 256 · 7×7 grid · 7 blocks · H 6 heads × d 32 per position · 25 Hz · 32.55M trainable · fixed state 2,107,441 values · input: the last 4 tokens on fixed rings · trained 256 ticks at a time, the state never reset
each block: 7 × (conv 3×3 + BN + ReLU) → 1×1 conv → u, then x′ = u + (delta-rule memory Δ read)
one block, zoomed in: pane B ▼
the sampled token → the next tick's input (training: the dataset's)
fixed rings: tokens t … t−3 onto the grid, one ring each
Δ: gated delta-rule memory update and read
D flip-flop register, clocked every tick
(S: never reset; it carries across documents)

g.text: B · one block (all 7 have this structure, each with its own weights and memory)

x: 256×7×7 per tick · H = 6 heads of d = 32 at each of the 49 positions · every operation is per position except the 3×3 convs · base windows exp(−λ), learned, starting log-spaced over the heads: 16 … 16,384 ticks
S ← α · S (I − β k kᵀ) + β v kᵀ
erase what k pointed at, write v there,
no weights of its own: S is state (fast weights),
learned only through the 1×1 convs feeding it
Training: everything before Δ runs on all
256 ticks of a window (32 rows) at once.
q, k, v, β, α for the window go to a
chunked scan (the WY form of the delta
rule, Yang et al. 2024), giving every S q
exactly. The state carries on between
windows; the gradient stops at a window's start.
Chip: one tick at a time. Per block it
Same results as training, by construction.
L2: q, k scaled to unit length per head (keeps S bounded)
gates: β = σ(·), α = exp(−2 exp(λ) σ(·)), λ per head
D flip-flop register, clocked every tick
(S: never reset; it carries across documents)
